text:
To every future RPN currently studying: I see you.

When I was preparing for the RPNCE, I felt like I was searching in the dark. Almost every study guide and resource out there was tailored for the NCLEX and RNs, leaving us RPNs to figure out the rest on our own.

That’s the real reason I started sharing my journey. I didn’t want anyone coming after me to feel that same isolation. If sharing my path helps make yours just a little lighter, clearer, or less scary—then every video is worth it.

Would it be helpful if I shared the exact study tools and resources I used to pass? Let me know in the comments! 👇

#RPNCE⁠ ⁠#RegisteredPsychiatricNurse⁠ ⁠#PsychiatricNursing⁠ ⁠#RPNStudent⁠ ⁠#CanadianNurse⁠ ⁠

text: Ever wonder if the RPN route is really worth it? Here’s the honest truth from someone who’s been in the trenches—working full-time, doing the same tasks as RNs, but for a whole lot less. 💬 This isn’t to bash anyone’s path. It’s to share one perspective. Because sometimes, choosing the "quicker" route can come with long-term trade-offs. Whether you’re choosing between RPN and RN, or feeling the pressure to “upgrade,” just know this: your path is still valid. You’re not behind. 👉 What’s been your experience? Drop it in the comments.
